title: WORKSHEET 21
subject: Tenses (Rewrite or Combine)
subjectVi: Ngữ pháp bài 21: Tenses (Rewrite or Combine)

sections.instruction: Change the tense of the following sentences using the given time expressions. (Example: They often play cards. → a) When I saw them, they were playing cards. b) for two hours → They have been playing cards for two hours.)

questions.prompt: They often play cards. — c) While we were studying maths,
acceptedAnswers: While we were studying maths, they were playing cards.
They were playing cards while we were studying maths.

questions.prompt: They often play cards. — d) three hours ago
acceptedAnswers: They played cards three hours ago.

questions.prompt: They often play cards. — e) on Saturday nights
acceptedAnswers: They play cards on Saturday nights.
On Saturday nights they play cards.

questions.prompt: They often play cards. — f) at the moment
acceptedAnswers: They are playing cards at the moment.
At the moment they are playing cards.

questions.prompt: John copies two cassettes every day. — a) since 8 o’clock
acceptedAnswers: John has copied two cassettes since 8 o’clock.
John has been copying cassettes since 8 o’clock.
John has been copying two cassettes since 8 o’clock.

questions.prompt: John copies two cassettes every day. — b) at present
acceptedAnswers: John is copying two cassettes at present.
At present John is copying two cassettes.

questions.prompt: John copies two cassettes every day. — c) next Saturday
acceptedAnswers: John is going to copy two cassettes next Saturday.
John will copy two cassettes next Saturday.
John is copying two cassettes next Saturday.

questions.prompt: John copies two cassettes every day. — d) already
acceptedAnswers: John has already copied two cassettes.

questions.prompt: John copies two cassettes every day. — e) yesterday
acceptedAnswers: John copied two cassettes yesterday.
Yesterday John copied two cassettes.

questions.prompt: Kathy is writing a letter now. — a) every two weeks
acceptedAnswers: Kathy writes a letter every two weeks.

questions.prompt: Kathy is writing a letter now. — b) while we were playing
acceptedAnswers: Kathy was writing a letter while we were playing.
While we were playing, Kathy was writing a letter.

questions.prompt: Kathy is writing a letter now. — c) when she is alone
acceptedAnswers: Kathy writes a letter when she is alone.
When she is alone, Kathy writes a letter.
Kathy writes letters when she is alone.

questions.prompt: Kathy is writing a letter now. — d) just
acceptedAnswers: Kathy has just written a letter.

questions.prompt: Kathy is writing a letter now. — e) next month
acceptedAnswers: Kathy is going to write a letter next month.
Kathy will write a letter next month.

questions.prompt: Kathy is writing a letter now. — f) last week
acceptedAnswers: Kathy wrote a letter last week.
Last week Kathy wrote a letter.

questions.prompt: He usually reads magazines. — a) for an hour
acceptedAnswers: He has been reading magazines for an hour.
He has read magazines for an hour.

questions.prompt: He usually reads magazines. — b) when I saw him
acceptedAnswers: He was reading magazines when I saw him.
When I saw him, he was reading magazines.

questions.prompt: He usually reads magazines. — c) every morning
acceptedAnswers: He reads magazines every morning.
Every morning he reads magazines.

questions.prompt: He usually reads magazines. — d) now
acceptedAnswers: He is reading magazines now.
Now he is reading magazines.

questions.prompt: He usually reads magazines. — e) yet
acceptedAnswers: He hasn’t read magazines yet.
He hasn’t read the magazines yet.
Has he read the magazines yet?

questions.prompt: The children are doing their homework. — a) yet
acceptedAnswers: The children haven’t done their homework yet.
Have the children done their homework yet?

questions.prompt: The children are doing their homework. — b) just
acceptedAnswers: The children have just done their homework.

questions.prompt: The children are doing their homework. — c) every evening
acceptedAnswers: The children do their homework every evening.
Every evening the children do their homework.

questions.prompt: The children are doing their homework. — d) when she came
acceptedAnswers: The children were doing their homework when she came.
When she came, the children were doing their homework.

sections.instruction: Read the passage and ask questions for the given answers:
sections.contextText:
Janet Johnson is a film actress. She made several animal films. She is talking about an elephant called HEKIMA.
“I met Hekima when I went to Africa seven years ago. We were in Tanzania and we were making a film about elephants. When we arrived, we saw three young elephants. They were playing together. Hekima was small, friendly and intelligent. We called her Hekima because it means ‘wisdom’. Hekima was a great actress, and the film made her famous. After we finished the film we left Africa. I thought I’d never see Hekima again. But she left Africa, too. She came to a zoo in the USA. I was working in New York when I heard about that. She was happy when she saw me. She was playing happily. I think she remembered me.”

questions.prompt: Janet went to Africa seven years ago.
acceptedAnswers: When did Janet go to Africa?
questions.explanation: past simple question: When did + subject + verb

questions.prompt: Janet was making a film in Tanzania.
acceptedAnswers: What was Janet making in Tanzania?
What was Janet doing in Tanzania?
Where was Janet making a film?
questions.explanation: past continuous question: wh- + was + subject + -ing

questions.prompt: The elephants were playing when they arrived.
acceptedAnswers: What were the elephants doing when they arrived?
questions.explanation: past continuous question: wh- + were + subject + -ing

questions.prompt: Because Hekima was an intelligent elephant.
acceptedAnswers: Why did they call her Hekima?
Why did they call the elephant Hekima?
Why was she called Hekima?
Why did Janet call her Hekima?

questions.prompt: It means “wisdom”.
acceptedAnswers: What does Hekima mean?
questions.explanation: present simple question: What does + subject + mean?

questions.prompt: Hekima was in a zoo in the USA while Janet was working in New York.
acceptedAnswers: Where was Hekima while Janet was working in New York?

questions.prompt: Hekima was playing when Janet went to see her.
acceptedAnswers: What was Hekima doing when Janet went to see her?
questions.explanation: past continuous question: What was + subject + doing?

sections.instruction: Match the sentences in A and B using WHILE and PAST CONTINUOUS / PAST SIMPLE: (Example: I burnt my finger while I was cooking the dinner.)
sections.contextText:
A:
1. I (burn) my finger.
2. I (break) a cup.
3. My car (break down).
4. I (see) a shark.
5. My clothes (get) dirty.
6. I (break) a tooth.

B:
I (drive) to work.
I (eat) a nut.
I (cook) the dinner.
I (do) the washing up.
I (swim) in the sea.
I (clean) my room.

questions.prompt: I (break) a cup.
acceptedAnswers: I broke a cup while I was doing the washing up.
While I was doing the washing up, I broke a cup.
questions.explanation: past simple (short action) + while + past continuous

questions.prompt: My car (break down).
acceptedAnswers: My car broke down while I was driving to work.
While I was driving to work, my car broke down.
questions.explanation: past simple (short action) + while + past continuous

questions.prompt: I (see) a shark.
acceptedAnswers: I saw a shark while I was swimming in the sea.
While I was swimming in the sea, I saw a shark.
questions.explanation: past simple (short action) + while + past continuous

questions.prompt: My clothes (get) dirty.
acceptedAnswers: My clothes got dirty while I was cleaning my room.
While I was cleaning my room, my clothes got dirty.
questions.explanation: past simple (short action) + while + past continuous

questions.prompt: I (break) a tooth.
acceptedAnswers: I broke a tooth while I was eating a nut.
While I was eating a nut, I broke a tooth.
questions.explanation: past simple (short action) + while + past continuous

sections.instruction: Use the correct form of the verbs:

questions.prompt: The Bartons [gap] (go) to the mountains last weekend.
acceptedAnswers: went

questions.prompt: While they [gap] (have) lunch, a man [gap] (fall) down the tree.
acceptedAnswers: were having / fell
questions.explanation: while + past continuous; interrupting action → past simple

questions.prompt: They [gap] (take) him to the hospital in their car.
acceptedAnswers: took

questions.prompt: They [gap] (visit) him twice in the hospital since that time.
acceptedAnswers: have visited

questions.prompt: The man [gap] (be) better now and the doctors say he [gap] (leave) the hospital soon.
acceptedAnswers: is / will leave|is going to leave|is leaving

questions.prompt: When the Bartons [gap] (visit) him yesterday, they [gap] (take) him a bunch of flowers.
acceptedAnswers: visited / took

questions.prompt: The man [gap] (be) very happy and [gap] (thank) them.
acceptedAnswers: was / thanked

questions.prompt: Mr. Barton now says he [gap] (spend) the next weekend at the seaside and he [gap] (hope) there [gap] (not / be) any more accidents.
acceptedAnswers: is going to spend|will spend|is spending / hopes / won't be|aren't going to be

questions.prompt: I [gap] (finish) school last month and I [gap] (not / have) a job yet, but fortunately I [gap] (have) a job interview tomorrow.
acceptedAnswers: finished / haven't got|don't have|haven't had / have|am having|have got
questions.explanation: last month → past; yet → present (perfect); tomorrow → arrangement

questions.prompt: I usually [gap] (get) up early so I often [gap] (sleep) at around half past ten.
acceptedAnswers: get / sleep|go to sleep

questions.prompt: I [gap] (be) a little excited last night and because of this I [gap] (want / watch) TV before I [gap] (go) to bed.
acceptedAnswers: was / wanted to watch / went
questions.explanation: last night → past simple; want + to-infinitive

questions.prompt: There [gap] (be) a film about birds on TV and while I [gap] (sit) on the sofa, I [gap] (fall) asleep.
acceptedAnswers: was / was sitting / fell
questions.explanation: while + past continuous; interrupting action → past simple

questions.prompt: [gap] you [gap] (have) a terrible dream?
acceptedAnswers: Have / had|ever had
Did / have|ever have

questions.prompt: Well, I [gap] (have) one last night.
acceptedAnswers: had

questions.prompt: In my dream I [gap] (be) a parrot and my flat [gap] (be) on the tenth floor of a big building.
acceptedAnswers: was / was

questions.prompt: A big cat [gap] (want / catch) me so I [gap] (begin / fly).
acceptedAnswers: wanted to catch / began to fly|began flying

questions.prompt: I [gap] (have) nowhere [gap] (go) because the door [gap] (be) locked.
acceptedAnswers: had / to go / was

questions.prompt: Suddenly the cat [gap] (attack) me.
acceptedAnswers: attacked

questions.prompt: It nearly [gap] (kill) me.
acceptedAnswers: killed

questions.prompt: While I [gap] (shout) in pain, a voice [gap] (say), “[gap] you [gap] (see) my books? I can’t find them.”
acceptedAnswers: was shouting / said / Have / seen
was shouting / said / Did / see
questions.explanation: while + past continuous; present perfect question

questions.prompt: When I [gap] (open) my eyes, I [gap] (feel) very happy [gap] (see) my sister.
acceptedAnswers: opened / felt / to see

questions.prompt: Of course she [gap] (not / understand) the reason but I [gap] (give) her a big kiss.
acceptedAnswers: didn't understand / gave

sections.instruction: REWRITE or COMBINE the following using the word in brackets:

questions.prompt: It rained this morning. The children played in the garden. (while)
acceptedAnswers: While it was raining this morning, the children were playing in the garden.
The children were playing in the garden while it was raining this morning.
The children played in the garden while it was raining this morning.

questions.prompt: What did you do? The doorbell rang. (when)
acceptedAnswers: What were you doing when the doorbell rang?
What did you do when the doorbell rang?
questions.explanation: past continuous interrupted by past simple

questions.prompt: I walked along Main Street. I realized a man behind me. (when)
acceptedAnswers: I was walking along Main Street when I realized a man behind me.
When I was walking along Main Street, I realized a man behind me.
I was walking along Main Street when I realised a man behind me.
questions.explanation: past continuous interrupted by past simple

questions.prompt: I started to play football when I was five. (since)
acceptedAnswers: I have played football since I was five.
I have been playing football since I was five.

questions.prompt: The windows are dirty. I last cleaned them last month. (since)
acceptedAnswers: I haven’t cleaned the windows since last month.
The windows are dirty. I haven’t cleaned them since last month.
The windows are dirty because I haven’t cleaned them since last month.
The windows haven’t been cleaned since last month.

questions.prompt: He last shaved a week ago. (for)
acceptedAnswers: He hasn’t shaved for a week.
questions.explanation: last did… ago → haven’t done… for

questions.prompt: Maybe the train leaves at six. I don’t catch it. (If)
acceptedAnswers: If the train leaves at six, I won’t catch it.
I won’t catch the train if it leaves at six.

questions.prompt: We slept last night. The robber stole all the jewellery. (as)
acceptedAnswers: As we were sleeping last night, the robber stole all the jewellery.
The robber stole all the jewellery as we were sleeping last night.
As we were sleeping last night, the robber stole all the jewelry.

questions.prompt: Tom prefers learning French to learning Japanese. (would rather)
acceptedAnswers: Tom would rather learn French than Japanese.
Tom would rather learn French than learn Japanese.

questions.prompt: Angela looks after many children. It keeps her busy. (Gerund)
acceptedAnswers: Looking after many children keeps Angela busy.
Looking after many children keeps her busy.

questions.prompt: He went to London. He wanted to work there. (to)
acceptedAnswers: He went to London to work there.
He went to London to work.

questions.prompt: They had a picnic. The forest caught fire. (as)
acceptedAnswers: As they were having a picnic, the forest caught fire.
The forest caught fire as they were having a picnic.

questions.prompt: No sound could be heard. The walls were very thick. (because)
acceptedAnswers: No sound could be heard because the walls were very thick.
Because the walls were very thick, no sound could be heard.

questions.prompt: My bed is terribly hard. I can’t sleep well. (so + adjective + that)
acceptedAnswers: My bed is so hard that I can’t sleep well.
My bed is so terribly hard that I can’t sleep well.

questions.prompt: The shopkeeper doesn’t let the children put their fingers on the glass while they are looking at the sweets. (be allowed to)
acceptedAnswers: The children aren’t allowed to put their fingers on the glass while they are looking at the sweets.
questions.explanation: let somebody do → be allowed to do

questions.prompt: My mother would rather cook than iron. (prefer)
acceptedAnswers: My mother prefers cooking to ironing.
My mother prefers to cook rather than iron.

questions.prompt: We bought this house in 1990. (since)
acceptedAnswers: We have had this house since 1990.
We have lived in this house since 1990.
We have owned this house since 1990.

questions.prompt: He may come late. He will call us. (If)
acceptedAnswers: If he comes late, he will call us.
He will call us if he comes late.

questions.prompt: Paris isn’t as crowded as New York. (comparison)
acceptedAnswers: New York is more crowded than Paris.
Paris is less crowded than New York.

questions.prompt: My father would rather read the newspaper than watch TV. (prefer)
acceptedAnswers: My father prefers reading the newspaper to watching TV.
My father prefers reading newspapers to watching TV.
My father prefers to read the newspaper rather than watch TV.

sections.instruction: Look at the chart and make sentences (past simple for yesterday, present continuous for today, will for tomorrow) as in the example: (Example: People traveled on horseback yesterday. People are traveling by plane today. People will travel in spaceships tomorrow.)

questions.prompt: children / play: hide-and-seek (yesterday) · computer games (today) · with robots (tomorrow)
acceptedAnswers: Children played hide-and-seek yesterday. Children are playing computer games today. Children will play with robots tomorrow.
Children played hide-and-seek yesterday. They are playing computer games today. They will play with robots tomorrow.
questions.explanation: yesterday → past; today → present continuous; tomorrow → will

questions.prompt: man / explore: the poles (yesterday) · the solar system (today) · galaxies (tomorrow)
acceptedAnswers: Man explored the poles yesterday. Man is exploring the solar system today. Man will explore galaxies tomorrow.
Man explored the poles yesterday. Man is exploring the solar system today. Man will explore the galaxies tomorrow.
questions.explanation: yesterday → past; today → present continuous; tomorrow → will

questions.prompt: we / live: in villages (yesterday) · in modern cities (today) · in undersea cities (tomorrow)
acceptedAnswers: We lived in villages yesterday. We are living in modern cities today. We will live in undersea cities tomorrow.
questions.explanation: yesterday → past; today → present continuous; tomorrow → will

questions.prompt: wives / use: handmade tools (yesterday) · electric appliances (today) · intelligent robots (tomorrow)
acceptedAnswers: Wives used handmade tools yesterday. Wives are using electric appliances today. Wives will use intelligent robots tomorrow.
Wives used handmade tools yesterday. They are using electric appliances today. They will use intelligent robots tomorrow.
questions.explanation: yesterday → past; today → present continuous; tomorrow → will

questions.prompt: vehicles / run: by horses (yesterday) · by petrol (today) · by water or electricity (tomorrow)
acceptedAnswers: Vehicles ran by horses yesterday. Vehicles are running by petrol today. Vehicles will run by water or electricity tomorrow.
Vehicles ran by horses yesterday. Vehicles are running by petrol today. Vehicles will run by water and electricity tomorrow.
Vehicles were run by horses yesterday. Vehicles are run by petrol today. Vehicles will be run by water or electricity tomorrow.
Vehicles ran by horses yesterday. Vehicles run by petrol today. Vehicles will run by water or electricity tomorrow.
questions.explanation: yesterday → past; today → present; tomorrow → will
